general_criteria.D1: The control description states who performs it, what they do, how often, and what evidence is retained.
general_criteria.D2: The control addresses the stated risk, at a level of precision that would prevent or detect the problem.
general_criteria.D3: The performer has the competence and authority to perform it.
general_criteria.D4: The performer is independent of the activity being controlled.
general_criteria.D5: The information the control relies on is complete and accurate, or a control exists that ensures it.
general_criteria.D6: Follow-up of items the control identifies is defined, including a timeframe.
general_criteria.D7: The walkthrough occurrence was performed as the description states.

modules.title: User access review
modules.risk: Users retain access that is unauthorized or no longer appropriate for their role, allowing unauthorized transactions or changes to financial data.
modules.population: The review instances in the period. Within each selected review, UAR-A to UAR-D are tested for the whole review. UAR-E and UAR-F cover every access change requested where the data allows testing by code; otherwise the means of selection is set in the rationale (section 5.5).

expectations.text: The review covers all account types (end user, privileged, service, shared) and every in-scope layer, or other tested controls cover the rest.
The review is based on a complete and accurate listing that shows access in a form the reviewer can understand.
Reviewers know the users' responsibilities, and no one certifies their own access.
The frequency and the completion timeframe are defined and suit the risk.
Changes requested are tracked until made in the system, within a defined timeframe.
Inappropriate access found is assessed for whether it was used.

attributes.text: The user listing was system-generated from production, covers all account types and access rights, and meets section 5.4.
Every account on the listing has a documented reviewer decision.
Each reviewer was appropriate under the control, and no reviewer certified their own access.
The review was completed and signed off within the timeframe the control defines.
Access marked for change or removal was changed in the system within the defined timeframe, verified against system evidence and not ticket closure alone.
For inappropriate access found, the assessment of whether it was used was performed and documented.

evidence: Access review policy or procedure.
For each selected review: the listing as used, with query or parameters, generation timestamp, and source record count.
HR listing of active employees and contractors, with manager and job title.
Reviewer assignments and sign-offs, with dates.
Changes requested, related tickets, and system evidence of each change with its date.
Records of any assessment of whether inappropriate access was used.

modules.title: Privileged access
modules.risk: Privileged access allows a user to bypass application controls, change data directly, or alter security settings without detection.
modules.population: Restriction: All privileged accounts at the test date. Activity monitoring: Review instances in the period. Emergency access: Emergency access uses in the period.

populations.population: All privileged accounts at the test date
populations.selection: PRIV-A, PRIV-B, PRIV-D by code over the full population. PRIV-C, PRIV-E, PRIV-F over the full population by default, or as the approved rationale sets for a large population.

populations.population: Emergency access uses in the period

expectations.text: "Privileged" is defined for each layer and captures every role or permission that gives administrative capability.
Every privileged account is attributable to a named individual or a documented owner.
Privileged access is granted on job need, with approval before it is granted.
Conflicting duties are prevented, or an alternative control addresses them.
Shared and default accounts are controlled.
Privileged activity is logged, the logs are protected from those whose activity they record, and the activity is independently reviewed.
Where emergency access is possible, it is approved, time-limited, and its activity reviewed.

attributes.text: The privileged account listing was system-generated, meets section 5.4, and includes every role or permission meeting the definition of privileged. The Tester documents how those roles were identified.
Each account maps to a named individual, or a documented owner for service and shared accounts.
Each individual is active per the HR listing and their job function supports the access.
Privileged users do not hold conflicting duties, or the alternative control identified in the design assessment covers the conflict.
Shared and default accounts are controlled as the control prescribes.
Privileged access granted in the period was approved by an authorized approver before it was granted.
Logging was enabled for privileged accounts for the period covered by the selected review.
The review was performed on time by a person independent of the activity reviewed.
Items identified were investigated and resolved, with the resolution documented.
The use had a documented business reason and was approved as the control requires.
Access was removed at the end of the approved window.
Activity during the window was reviewed on time by an independent person.

evidence: Privileged access policy and the definition of privileged roles per layer.
System-generated listing of accounts with privileged roles, with generation evidence.
HR listing with job titles; request and approval records for access granted in the period.
Password vault configuration and shared account inventory.
Logging configuration, log review sign-offs, and follow-up records.
Emergency access log, approvals, and activity reviews.

modules.title: Change management
modules.risk: Unauthorized, untested, or inappropriate changes cause incorrect processing of financial data or undermine automated controls and reports.
modules.population: The population should be a system-generated list of changes actually made in production (for example a transport log, deployment history, or merge history). A ticketing system list contains only changes that followed the process, so it cannot show completeness alone. If it is the only list available, the Tester proposes an alternative procedure under section 5.4, normally reconciling a system change log or object modification dates to the tickets. A production change with no ticket is recorded as an exception and evaluated. Emergency changes and direct data changes are normally tested as a targeted selection in addition to the sample (section 5.5).

expectations.text: All change types are covered: code, configuration, database, infrastructure, emergency, vendor, and direct data changes.
Every production change is requested, documented, and traceable to its request.
Changes are tested before migration, to an extent that suits their nature.
Migration is approved beforehand by an authorized approver.
Developing and migrating are separated: enforced by the system, monitored, or addressed by an alternative control.
Emergency changes follow a defined procedure with a timeframe for approval after the fact.
Development, test, and production environments are separate.

attributes.text: The production change traces to a documented change request.
Testing was performed and documented before migration, in line with the nature of the change and by the party the control requires.
Migration was approved by an authorized approver, and the approval precedes the production implementation.
The person who migrated the change is not the developer, and the approver is not the developer, or the alternative control identified in the design assessment covers it.
For an emergency change: the emergency procedure was followed and approval after the fact was obtained within the defined timeframe.
No user has both development access and production migration access, or the overlap is covered by a monitoring control that is tested and effective.
attributes.group: full population, at the test date

evidence: Change management policy and the list of authorized approvers.
System-generated production change log for the period, with generation evidence.
For each selected change: ticket, test evidence, approval with timestamp, and deployment record with timestamp and deploying user.
User listings for development access and for production migration access.

modules.title: Job monitoring
modules.risk: Failures of, or unauthorized changes to, scheduled jobs and interfaces that process financial data go undetected or unresolved, leaving financial data incomplete or inaccurate.
modules.population: Failure resolution: Failures of in-scope jobs in the period, from the scheduler log. Daily monitoring: Days in the period. Automated alerting: The alert configuration. Schedule changes: Schedule changes in the period, from the scheduler audit log.

populations.population: Failures of in-scope jobs in the period, from the scheduler log
populations.selection: Per the rationale; failures near period-end are normally a targeted selection

populations.population: Schedule changes in the period, from the scheduler audit log

expectations.text: An inventory identifies the financially relevant jobs and is kept current.
Failures are detected promptly, by operator monitoring, automated alerting, or both.
Failures are investigated and resolved, and the effect on downstream processing is assessed.
Data corrections made to resolve a failure follow the change procedure.
Changes to job schedules are authorized.
Access to the scheduler is restricted.

attributes.text: The in-scope job inventory agrees to the scheduler configuration, and the failure log is system-generated for the full period and meets section 5.4.
The failure was detected and logged within the timeframe the control defines.
The cause and the action taken were documented.
The job was rerun successfully or otherwise resolved, verified against the scheduler's completion record and not ticket closure alone.
Where resolution required a data correction or schedule change, it followed the applicable change procedure.
The review for the selected day was performed and signed off by the assigned operator on time.
The failures recorded in the review agree to the scheduler log for that day.
Each failure on that day has a ticket or documented follow-up.
Alerting is enabled for all in-scope jobs and sends to an appropriate, current distribution list.
The alert configuration was unchanged in the period, or changes followed change management.
Each selected schedule change traces to an approved change request, tested under CHG-A to CHG-D.

evidence: Job inventory with financial relevance, and the scheduler configuration export.
System-generated job run history for the period, with generation evidence.
Incident tickets and rerun records for selected failures.
Daily review checklists or sign-offs.
Alert configuration and distribution list membership.
Scheduler audit log of schedule changes.

modules.title: User provisioning and access changes
modules.risk: Access to financially relevant systems is granted, or changed, without authorization or beyond what the job requires, allowing unauthorized transactions or changes to financial data.
modules.population: All grants and changes of effective access in the period, assembled from every path in PROV-DE1: application role assignment logs, database and operating system account creation, directory group membership changes including nested groups, identity provider assignment logs, automated provisioning logs, and bulk load records. A list from the request system is not an acceptable population alone (section 5.4). The combined system-side population is reconciled to the request records, and a grant with no request is recorded as an exception. Where a path has no change log, the approved alternative under section 5.4 is normally a comparison of effective access at two dates, resolved through groups and inheritance, with every difference treated as a grant to be traced. Where the data allows, PROV-C and PROV-D are tested by code over the full population.

expectations.text: Every path by which effective access can be granted or changed goes through the request-and-approval process, or is covered by an alternative control. The paths include: direct assignment of application roles; database and operating system accounts; accounts and roles assigned directly by administrators outside the request tool; group-based access, where membership of a directory or application group confers roles; inherited access through nested groups, role hierarchies, or parent roles; federated access assigned in an identity provider and pushed to the application; automated provisioning from HR or identity attributes; temporary or time-boxed grants; and bulk loads or migrations.
The approver is defined and appropriate (the user's manager, the system or data owner, or both), and no one approves their own access.
Approval precedes the grant.
The access granted is the access approved, measured as effective access after groups, nesting, and inheritance are resolved.

Role and permission definitions exist so that approvers understand what they approve, including what a group or parent role confers, and conflicting combinations are checked before granting where the application supports conflicts.
Where provisioning is automated from identity or HR attributes, the rule set is approved and changes to it follow change management.
Temporary and time-boxed grants are approved, expire or are removed at the end of the approved window, and are distinguished from emergency privileged access (AC-PRIV).

attributes.text: The population is assembled from every path in PROV-DE1, is system-generated from production, resolves group-based and inherited access to effective access, meets section 5.4, and is reconciled to the request records.
The access was requested and approved by an appropriate approver under the control, and the approver is not the user.
The approval precedes the grant, by timestamp, with both timestamps on a common time basis.
The effective access granted in the system matches the access approved.
Where the control requires it, a conflict check was performed before granting, and any conflict was resolved or accepted by an authorized person.

For automated provisioning: the rule set is approved, each rule's output matches the HR or identity attributes it depends on (tested once per rule), and changes to the rules in the period followed change management.
Each temporary or time-boxed grant was approved, and the access expired or was removed at the end of the approved window, per system evidence.

evidence: Access management policy, approver matrix, and role, group, and permission definitions, including group-to-role mappings and role hierarchies.

System-generated logs for each path: application role assignments, account creation, directory group changes, identity provider assignments, automated provisioning, and bulk loads, each with generation evidence.
Request records with approvals and timestamps, and the time zone basis of each source.
HR listing with manager and job title.
Identity system rule configuration and its change log.
Temporary grant records with approved windows.

modules.title: Termination and transfer
modules.risk: People who have left the company or moved roles retain access, allowing unauthorized access or transactions, including by former employees.
modules.population: All terminations and transfers in the period, from each system of record identified under TERM-DE1, not from IT tickets. Where the system-of-record listing and the system account listing are both available, TERM-B is tested by code over the full population.

expectations.text: The trigger is reliable: termination and transfer data flows from the system of record to the people who disable access, and it covers employees, contractors, and third-party users. Where contractors and third parties are not in HR, a separate system of record (vendor management, contract end dates, a contractor register) is identified.

The timeframe for disabling is defined and suits the risk, and the control defines the event the timeframe runs from: the last working day, the effective termination date and time, or the date HR processes the leaver.
Disabling covers every in-scope layer and every entry point: directory and single sign-on, remote access, federated identities, and application accounts that are not integrated with single sign-on.
Disabling is confirmed from the system's own record of the disable event, not by ticket closure.
On transfer, prior access is reviewed and unneeded access removed within a defined timeframe.
A periodic reconciliation of active accounts to the active population in each system of record detects any termination that was missed.
Activity after the termination date is investigated when it occurs, using activity data whose meaning in that system is understood.

attributes.text: The termination and transfer listing is system-generated from each system of record, meets section 5.4, and covers employees, contractors, and third-party users.
For each termination, the actual disable or removal timestamp in each in-scope system, from that system's own record, is on or before the deadline computed under the rule above.

Post-termination activity investigation: any authentication or activity after the triggering event, identified from system-specific metadata whose meaning is understood (for example, the difference between a last-logon field updated by interactive logon and one updated by background processes or replication), is investigated and explained. This attribute records exposure; it is a deviation of the disabling control only where the control's own requirement was not met.
For each transfer, access no longer required was removed within the defined timeframe, as determined by the receiving manager.
Where the control depends on notification, the notification was sent and received within the defined timeframe.
The reconciliation of active accounts to each system of record was performed at the defined frequency, and discrepancies were resolved.

evidence: Termination and transfer listings for the period from HR and from any separate contractor or third-party system of record, with generation evidence and the field used as the triggering event.
System account listings for each in-scope layer with status, the system's disable or removal timestamp, and the logon metadata fields with their definitions.
The time zone configuration of each source.
Termination notifications or tickets.
Reconciliation records and resolution of discrepancies.

modules.title: Authentication and password configuration
modules.risk: Weak authentication allows a person other than the account holder to use an account, undermining every access control that depends on knowing who acted.
modules.population: The authentication configuration of each in-scope layer and of the identity provider. This is an automated control and is tested once per configuration under section 5.5, together with the configuration change log, the exempt accounts, and the bypass paths.

expectations.text: A policy defines the parameters for each layer, and the parameters are commensurate with the risk associated with the system and with the way it is reached (internal, remote, privileged, programmatic).
The parameters are enforced by system configuration rather than by user compliance, and accounts exempt from them are documented, approved, and covered by other measures.
The configuration is protected: changes follow change management, and access to security settings is restricted (AC-PRIV).

Where identity federation or single sign-on is used, the identity provider's authentication configuration and the trust relationship to each application are in scope. Paths that bypass the identity provider are identified and controlled: local application accounts, legacy or basic authentication protocols, direct database and operating system logons, API keys and service credentials, and break-glass accounts.

attributes.text: The configuration, inspected directly in production for each in-scope layer and the identity provider, agrees to the policy for every parameter.
The configuration was unchanged during the period per the audit log, or each change followed change management.
Accounts exempt from the parameters, identified from the system rather than from a maintained list, are documented, approved, and covered by other measures.

Multi-factor authentication is enforced, not merely enrolled: the enforcement policy or conditional access rule covers the in-scope population with no uncontrolled exclusions, and authentication logs for the period show no successful single-factor logon by an account the policy covers.
Local accounts and federated identities that bypass or sit outside the identity provider are identified from the system and are controlled under this module or AC-PRIV.

Bypass paths (legacy or basic authentication protocols, direct database and operating system logons, API and service credentials, break-glass accounts) are disabled, restricted to identified accounts, or monitored, per configuration and logs.

evidence: Authentication policy and the design rationale for its parameters.
Configuration exports, or screenshots meeting section 5.3, for each layer and the identity provider, including trust and federation settings.
Configuration change log for the period.
Listing of accounts with non-expiring passwords or other exemptions.
Multi-factor enforcement policy configuration, its exclusion lists, and authentication logs showing the factor used.
Settings and logs for legacy protocols, API credentials, and break-glass accounts.

modules.title: Physical access to computing facilities
modules.risk: Unauthorized physical access to servers, storage, media, or network devices allows logical controls to be bypassed, or data to be taken, altered, or destroyed.
modules.population: For each company-controlled location: all people with access at the test date, from the access control system; review instances in the period; terminations in the period; visitor log entries in the period.

expectations.text: Access to each company-controlled location is granted only on approval to people with a job need.
The access list for each location is reviewed periodically.
Access is removed on termination or transfer.
Visitors are logged and escorted.

For locations shared with a provider, the company's part of the arrangement (its own badge lists, cage or rack keys, media handling, and the user entity controls the provider's report assumes) is identified and controlled.

attributes.text: The access listing is system-generated from the access control system for each location and meets section 5.4.
Each person with access is active per the HR or contractor listing and has a job need, with approval for access granted in the period.
The periodic review was performed on time by an appropriate person, and changes were made.
Access for people terminated in the period was removed within the defined timeframe, per access control system evidence, using the deadline rule in module AC-TERM.
Visitor log entries show sign-in, sign-out, and an escort.

evidence: The location inventory and shared-responsibility arrangement for each system.
Access control system listing with generation evidence; access approvals.
Review records; termination listing; removal dates.
Visitor logs.
For shared locations, the provider's report and the mapping of the company's responsibilities (TP-SOC1).

modules.title: Direct data changes
modules.risk: Data in production is changed directly, by scripts, database updates, data-fix utilities, or debug modes, bypassing application controls and allowing misstatement or concealment.
modules.population: All direct changes in the period. The preferred source is a system-recorded log: a database audit log, an application table-change log, or a privileged session log. Approved alternative sources, under section 5.4, include database transaction logs, change-data-capture records, privileged session recordings, comparison of table snapshots at two dates, and the request system reconciled against privileged activity logs, where the engagement approver judges the source gives sufficient assurance of completeness.

expectations.text: Every path for direct change is identified: database updates, scripts, application data-fix transactions, mass uploads, and changes made by a vendor. The ability to use each path is restricted (AC-PRIV), and the company has a means of knowing what direct changes occurred, by logging or by another detective mechanism.
The business or data owner approves before execution.
The change is reviewed before execution, including the records expected to be affected, and run in a non-production environment first where feasible.
The person executing is authorized and is not the requester, and the before-and-after state is retained and confirmed against the approval.

The population of direct changes comes from a system-recorded source, or from an approved alternative source that gives sufficient assurance of completeness; the request system alone is not sufficient.
The financial effect of the change is assessed, and changes that affect accounting records are routed to the accounting review that journal entries receive.

attributes.text: The population comes from a system-recorded source or an approved alternative source, meets section 5.4, and is reconciled to the request records; a change with no request is recorded as an exception.
The business or data owner approved the change before it was executed, by timestamp.
Review evidence before execution shows the expected effect, including record counts.
The executor is authorized and is not the requester, and the before-and-after evidence agrees to the approved change in records and values.
The financial effect was assessed, and the change was routed to accounting review where required.

evidence: Database, application, or privileged activity logs of direct changes, with generation evidence, or the approved alternative source.
Request and approval records; scripts or change specifications.
Before-and-after extracts; execution records with the executing user.
Approver list.

modules.title: System development, implementation, and data migration
modules.risk: A new or significantly changed system goes into production without adequate design, testing, approval, or accurate data conversion, producing incorrect processing or incomplete or inaccurate data.
modules.population: Each qualifying project or wave in the period. Every project is identified and assessed; the extent of attribute testing within a project follows the risk assessment. Within DEV-C, the reconciliations themselves form a population, and the means of selection among them is set under section 5.5.

expectations.text: A life-cycle methodology defines what must be produced and approved before release, in a form suited to the delivery model, and applies to vendor-delivered and hosted systems.
Requirements, including financial reporting requirements, automated controls, and key reports, are defined and approved in whatever form the delivery model uses.

Testing, including user acceptance by business users, is performed with documented results to an extent that suits the risk of the change, and defects are resolved or formally accepted before go-live.
Data migration follows an approved mapping, with trial conversions where the risk warrants, reconciliation of record counts and balances from source to target, resolution of exceptions, and sign-off.
Go-live is approved by authorized business and IT owners against a cut-over plan; a rollback or recovery option exists where the risk assessment calls for one.
Security configuration and segregation of duties are designed and reviewed before go-live, and implementers' access to production is removed afterwards.
Key reports, automated controls, and interfaces are validated in production after go-live.
A project risk assessment, approved before testing, sets which expectations apply and the extent of each.

attributes.text: Approved requirements and design exist, in the form the delivery model uses, and include the financial reporting requirements.
Test evidence exists to the extent the risk assessment sets, user acceptance was signed off by business users before go-live, and open defects were assessed and accepted.

The migration reconciliation agrees record counts and balances from source to target, with exceptions resolved and signed off; the Tester re-performs the reconciliations selected under section 5.5 on the extracts provided.
Go-live was approved by the authorized owners before the cut-over date, and the rollback or recovery option the risk assessment called for existed.
The security and segregation-of-duties design was reviewed, and implementer access to production was removed after go-live, per the account listing.
Post-go-live validation of key reports, automated controls, and interfaces is documented.

evidence: Project inventory; project charter, methodology, requirements, or backlog with acceptance criteria; design approvals.
Test plans, results, automated test records, defect logs, and user acceptance sign-offs.
Migration mapping, reconciliations, exception resolutions, and sign-offs, with source and target extracts.
Go-live or release approvals, the cut-over plan, and the rollback plan where required.
Production account listings before and after go-live; post-go-live validation records.
For software-as-a-service: the vendor's report (TP-SOC1) and the company's configuration and integration records.

modules.title: Backup and restoration
modules.risk: Financial data is lost or cannot be recovered after a failure, leaving records incomplete or the close unable to proceed.
modules.population: The backup configuration; backup failures in the period, from the backup tool's log; restoration tests in the period.

expectations.text: In-scope applications, databases, and configuration are in the backup schedule, at the frequency and retention the policy defines.
Backup failures are detected and resolved, in the same way as job failures.
Restoration is tested at a defined frequency, on in-scope data, with documented results.
Backup copies are stored separately from production and access to them is restricted (AC-PRIV).
For hosted systems, the company's own responsibilities, such as retention and restoration settings, are configured, and the provider's are covered under TP-SOC1.
Recovery objectives are defined with reference to financial reporting needs, including the close timetable.

attributes.text: The backup configuration, inspected directly, covers the in-scope systems at the policy frequency and retention, consistent with the recovery objectives.
Backup failures in the period, from a log that meets section 5.4, were resolved under JOB-B to JOB-D.
Restoration tests were performed at the defined frequency, on in-scope data, within the recovery objectives, with success documented or failures remediated.
Backup storage is separate from production, and access to it is restricted to authorized people.

evidence: Backup policy and recovery objectives; backup tool configuration and job history, with generation evidence.
Failure tickets and resolutions.
Restoration test records.
Storage configuration and access listing.
For hosted systems, the provider's report (TP-SOC1) and the company's settings.

modules.title: Incident and problem management
modules.risk: Incidents affecting in-scope systems, such as outages, processing errors, and security events, are not identified, resolved, or assessed for their effect on financial data, leaving errors uncorrected.
modules.population: Incidents on in-scope systems in the period, from the incident system. Because the incident system is the system of record for the control it cannot prove its own completeness, so completeness is tested by comparison to independent sources of incident indications. The sources available are recorded, and the comparison covers those the Planner judges relevant: A matter found in these sources with no incident record is recorded as an exception against INC-A and assessed. All major incidents affecting in-scope systems are a targeted selection; other incidents follow the selection rationale. Monitoring and alerting tools, and job failure logs (CO-JOB). Security tooling, such as event management and endpoint alerts. Emergency changes and direct data changes (CM-CHG, CM-DATA), which often follow an incident. Service desk channels outside the incident tool: email, chat, telephone logs. Vendor and hosting provider notifications and status pages. System availability and restart logs. Issues reported by finance during the close. Management reporting on availability and service levels.

expectations.text: Incidents are logged in a system with classification and priority, and the in-scope systems are identifiable in it.
Incidents are resolved within the timeframes defined for their priority, with the resolution documented.
Incidents affecting financial data are assessed for completeness and accuracy effects and communicated to finance, and corrections follow CM-DATA or CM-CHG.
Security incidents are escalated under the policy and assessed for their effect on ICFR.
Major incidents receive root cause analysis, and recurring incidents are analysed.

Every intake channel feeds the incident system, and the classification distinguishes incidents from service requests, so that incidents are not recorded elsewhere or under a category that escapes the control.

attributes.text: The incident extract meets section 5.4, and its completeness is supported by comparison to the independent sources recorded for the engagement, including sources beyond job failures.
The incident was classified and resolved within the defined timeframe, with the resolution documented.
Where financial data was affected, the effect was assessed and communicated, and any correction followed the applicable change procedure.
Each major incident has a root cause analysis with actions.
Each security incident was escalated under the policy and its effect on ICFR assessed.

evidence: Incident and problem management policy, including intake channels and classification rules.
Incident extract for the period, with generation evidence.

The independent sources listed above, as available: monitoring alerts, job failure logs, security alerts, emergency and data-change records, service desk channel logs, vendor notifications, availability logs, finance-reported issues, service-level reports.
Root cause analyses; communications to finance; related change or data-fix records.

modules.title: Service organizations and service auditor reports
modules.risk: Controls at a service organization that processes or hosts financial data are ineffective, or the company does not perform the controls the service organization's design assumes, and the company has no basis for relying on either.
modules.population: Every service organization in the inventory. All are assessed; sampling does not apply. The extent of work on each follows its risk assessment.

expectations.text: An inventory identifies every service organization relevant to ICFR, including hosting, software-as-a-service, and payroll, and maps each to the services used and the in-scope systems.
Evidence of the operating effectiveness of the relevant controls is obtained for each service organization from sources suited to its risk, and the period to the as-of date is covered.
A competent person reviews each item of evidence for what it covers, the period, the results, and the reliability of its source, and documents conclusions.
Complementary user entity controls, and any other controls the evidence assumes the company performs, are mapped to the company's own controls, which are in place and tested (AS 2201.B22).
Exceptions and deviations in the evidence are evaluated for their effect on the company's financial reporting, with management's response documented.
Subservice organizations carved out of a report are identified, and those relevant to the services used are covered by their own evidence or by the company's controls.
Where adequate evidence is not obtainable, management performs alternative procedures and, failing those, decides whether the inability means ICFR is not effective.
A risk assessment for each service organization, covering the seven points above, is recorded and approved before the evidence is evaluated.

attributes.text: The service organization is in the inventory, with its services, the in-scope systems, and the degree of interaction recorded.

The evidence obtained matches the risk assessment: its type, what it covers, its period and relation to the as-of date, and the coverage of the period to the as-of date are recorded, and any shortfall is addressed by alternative procedures or by management's decision under SOC-DE7.

For a service auditor's report: the opinion is unqualified, or any qualification is evaluated; the scope covers the services, locations, and systems the company uses; the controls tested relate to the company's relevant risks; and the service auditor's reputation, competence, and independence were considered.
Each exception or deviation in the evidence is identified, assessed for relevance to the company's use, and documented with a conclusion and management's response.
Each complementary user entity control, and any other control the evidence assumes, is mapped to a company control, and each mapped control is tested and effective, or the gap is evaluated.
Subservice organizations relevant to the services used are identified, and their evidence is obtained and reviewed, or the company's controls over them are documented.
The review was performed by a competent person, documented, and completed in time for management's assessment.
The risk assessment is documented, approved, and consistent with the evidence obtained and the extent of review.

evidence: Service organization inventory, contracts, and the risk assessment for each.
Service auditor reports of any type, agreed-upon procedures reports, bridge letters, and management's review memoranda.
Records of the company's own controls over each service and their test results.
Complementary user entity control mapping and the test results for the mapped controls.
Subservice organization reports or the company's controls over them.
Correspondence with the service organization about changes in the gap period.
